payload.task_text:
The e-commerce manager wants a monthly sales performance presentation to share with stakeholders and needs a planning meeting scheduled. Analyze WooCommerce order data broken down by month to compute monthly revenue totals and order counts across all order statuses.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx with the following slides. Slide 1 should be a title slide with "Monthly Sales Performance Review" as the title. Slide 2 should be titled "Monthly Revenue Overview" and contain a table showing each month (January through December), the number of orders, and the total revenue for that month. Slide 3 should be titled "Order Volume Trends" and describe the monthly order volume patterns. Slide 4 should be titled "Key Insights" and highlight the peak revenue month, the lowest revenue month, and total annual revenue. Slide 5 should be titled "Next Steps" with planned actions for improving sales performance.

Schedule a Google Calendar event called "Monthly Sales Review" on 2026-04-15 from 14:00 to 15:00 with a description noting it is a stakeholder review of monthly sales performance.

Email the presentation to ecommerce_manager@store.com with subject "Monthly Sales Performance Review" and include the key revenue highlights in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The complete order catalog, twelve monthly rows, five-slide deck, one fixed meeting, and one email form one compact workflow.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. Start the independent meeting inventory and order retrieval in the same response: call `list_events(timeMin="2026-04-15T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-04-16T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime")`, and call `woo_orders_list(perPage=100,page=1)` without `status`. Continue increasing order pages until a short or empty page, preserving all observed statuses; do not query by status/month and do not modify orders. Parse every observed order date and numeric total once, aggregate January through December counts and revenue including zero months, and freeze peak month, lowest month, and annual revenue with deterministic source-order tie handling.

Create `Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx` exactly once with one presentation ID and exactly the five requested slides, including all twelve monthly rows and insights derived only from the frozen table; read back the full slide inventory and verify every title/value. Filter the event inventory locally to exact `Monthly Sales Review` at 14:00–15:00, create once only if missing with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime` and description, retain the created/reused ID, and call `get_event`. Only after deck and event readback, check Sent mail for the exact recipient/subject; send one missing email with verified highlights and the presentation in the supported workspace-path `attachments` list, never retry an ambiguous send, and read back the attachment record before `claim_done`.

nodes.text:
You are analyzing WooCommerce order data to support a monthly sales performance report. This is a READ-ONLY analysis task — do not create, update, or delete anything.

DATA SOURCE: Use mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list with perPage=100 and paginate through ALL pages (page=1, 2, 3, ... continue until a page returns fewer than 100 items or an empty list). Do NOT pass a status filter — include every order regardless of status. Note: order the listing by date ascending or descending as convenient; just make sure you capture every order.

DELIVERABLES — return exactly this summary in your final message (compact, no raw order dumps):

1. SCOPE: Total number of orders fetched; the distinct years present in the data; earliest and latest order date_created.
2. MONTHLY TABLE: For each year-month (YYYY-MM) present, in chronological order: number of orders and total revenue (sum of each order's `total` field, 2 decimal places).
3. STATUS DISTRIBUTION: count of orders per status (e.g., completed, processing, on-hold, cancelled, refunded, failed, pending, trash — whatever appears).
4. HIGHLIGHTS: Peak revenue month (name + amount), lowest revenue month (name + amount), grand total revenue across ALL fetched orders, total order count, and average monthly order count.
5. CURRENCY: call mcp__woocommerce__woo_settings_get with groupId="general" once to report the store currency symbol/code.

Notes on methodology:
- Group orders by the calendar month of their `date_created` (or date_created_gmt — state which you used).
- Revenue per month = simple sum of the order `total` values, including all statuses (do not exclude cancelled/refunded/failed orders — the requirement is "across all order statuses").
- If data spans multiple years, still give the per-year-month breakdown and clearly label each month with its year.

Constraints: read-only tools only; keep your reply to the structured summary above.
Analyze WooCommerce monthly orders

TASK: Create a PowerPoint presentation file named Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx and save it at exactly this path:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-wc-order-monthly-ppt-gcal/workspace/Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx

Use the pptx MCP tools (create_presentation, add_slide, populate_placeholder/manage_text, add_table, save_presentation). Apply clean professional business styling (e.g., modern_blue color scheme). The deck must have EXACTLY 5 slides, in order, with these EXACT slide titles (copy them verbatim):

SLIDE 1 — Title slide
- Title (exact): "Monthly Sales Performance Review"
- Subtitle: "Stakeholder Briefing • March 2026" (optionally add "E-commerce Team" as a second line)

SLIDE 2 — Title (exact): "Monthly Revenue Overview"
- Add a table of 13 rows x 3 columns (header row + 12 month rows). Header: Month | Number of Orders | Total Revenue ($)
- Data rows EXACTLY as follows:
  January | 14 | $5,938.09
  February | 13 | $5,615.02
  March | 14 | $2,089.69
  April | 9 | $4,349.71
  May | 10 | $6,023.29
  June | 11 | $9,555.69
  July | 8 | $3,921.19
  August | 17 | $3,873.37
  September | 17 | $5,842.43
  October | 11 | $4,447.76
  November | 9 | $1,212.05
  December | 17 | $8,843.75
- Below or beside the table add one small note line: "150 orders, $61,712.04 total (Mar 2025 - Mar 2026; March includes partial 2026 data). All order statuses included."

SLIDE 3 — Title (exact): "Order Volume Trends"
Content bullets:
- Average of 12.5 orders per month across 150 total orders.
- Peak volume months: August, September, and December - 17 orders each.
- Quietest months: July (8) and November (9) orders.
- Spring was steady (Apr-Jun: 9-11 orders/month), July dipped, sharp rebound in Aug-Sep.
- Q4 close: December rebounded to 17 orders with the second-highest revenue ($8,843.75).
- Q1 2026 held momentum: January 14 and February 13 orders.

SLIDE 4 — Title (exact): "Key Insights"
Content bullets:
- Peak revenue month: June - $9,555.69.
- Strong seasonal close: December - $8,843.75 on the highest order volume (17 orders).
- Lowest revenue month: November - $1,212.05.
- Total revenue: $61,712.04 across 150 orders (Mar 2025 - Mar 2026, all order statuses).
- Volume does not equal revenue: Aug/Sep led volume but only mid-range revenue; June/December won on larger order values.
- Average monthly revenue: about $5,143.

SLIDE 5 — Title (exact): "Next Steps"
Content bullets:
- Plan promotions and inventory ahead of proven high-revenue windows (June, December).
- Target soft months (July, November) with targeted campaigns and bundles.
- Accelerate 56 open orders (processing, on-hold, pending) to convert pipeline into revenue.
- Analyze causes of 17 refunded/cancelled orders to recover lost revenue.
- Set a monthly revenue target (~$5,150) and track progress in monthly stakeholder reviews.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. File saved at the exact path above.
2. Exactly 5 slides; each slide title matches the required text exactly (including capitalization).
3. Slide 2 table contains all 12 months January-December with the exact order counts and revenue figures listed above, plus a header row.
4. No extra slides, no placeholder text left behind.

RETURN in your final message: the saved file path, the slide count, and a re-extracted listing of each slide's title (extract_presentation_text or equivalent) so the titles can be verified.
